Introduction

G-Cloud 15 is an online digital platform that helps public sector customers to buy commoditised cloud-based solutions through an open framework that will be reopened at 18 and 36 months allowing Suppliers to provide our customers with up-to-date innovative solutions and allowing new suppliers to join. Please see key changes between G-Cloud 14 to G-Cloud 15.
Purpose of document

The G-Cloud 15 Supplier guide contains post award information to enable you to constructively engage with Government Commercial Agency and public sector Buyers, as well as how to successfully manage your G-Cloud 15 digital platform items (service offers) through the digital marketplace (applytosupply)on the Digital platform once the agreement is live.

This guidance provides an overview of the agreement scope and sets out your contractual obligations including but not limited to MI reporting, management charges, assurance and audits which you should familiarise yourself with.
In addition, the guidance explains what theDigital platform is and describes the relevant processes around managing company and digital platform items (service offers) on the Digital platform.

Please note that this document is intended as additional guidance information and should not be consideredas an alternative to reading and understanding the framework agreement itself and all its schedules and annexes.
What is G-Cloud 15?
G-Cloud 15 replaces G-Cloud 14 and is an online catalogue hosted on the
Digital platform (Digital Marketplace). It provides a large range of cloud based services from a vast pool of Suppliers.
Who can access this agreement?

UK public sector bodies which include central government departments andtheir arm’s length bodies and agencies, non departmental public bodies,British overseas territories, and crown dependencies, NHS bodies, localauthorities and universities.
Full details can be found in thecontractnotice.

Agreement available for all UK public sector organisations to procure from
Services can be procured with Competitive Selection Process (previously further competition) and without competition (previously direct award)

Exclusions to G-Cloud 15 scope

G-Cloud 15 is not a contingent labour agreement and any requirements for contingent labour must be sourced through GCA’sWorkforce Solutions or Non Clinical Staffing. For clarity the services excluded from G-Cloud 15 include:
Co-location services - see Crown Hosting Services RM6262
Non-cloud related services / consultancy – see Technology Services 4 RM6190, Non Clinical Staffing RM6277 or Management Consultancy 4 RM6309
Bespoke design and development – see Digital Outcomes 7 RM1043.9
Hardware – see Technology Products & Associated Services 2 RM6098 and Vertical Application Solutions RM6259
Recruitment – only support relatingto the cloud is permitted, not the provision of staff or interims
Suppliers
You can find a list of suppliers in theA-Z list.

This agreement is an openframework. An open framework allows suppliers to join at multiple points throughout its duration. This framework will re-open after 18 months and again at 36 months. This allows suppliers to submit new bids to refresh existing Digital Platform Items (service offers) and pricing, add new services, and allow new suppliers to bid to join the framework. An existing supplier who submits new bids, or a new supplier bidding to join the framework, will be assessed on the same basis as the first framework within thescheme of open frameworks. Any changes made will be reassessed.
Pricing

G-Cloud 15 supports both Award Without Competition (formally referred to as Direct Award) and a Competitive Selection Process (sometimes referred to as award with competition and formerly known as Further Competition), procured in accordance with theProcurement Act 2023. These regulations state that in order for a Buyer to place an Award Without Competition, they must be presented with all of the necessary commercial information in a clear, open and transparent way, so that the Buyer can determine which is the most advantageous service that meets their needs. The Digital Platform Items (service offers) information is to include the service description including all associated pricing.
Pricing principles are set out in Framework Schedule 13 (pricing) more information can be found within theG-Cloud 15 Supplier information video: pricing

Buying process
Pre-procedure standard activity
Statement of Requirements
No matter the procedure, all Buyers willneed to develop a Statement of Requirements (SOR). In the case of complex requirements, this SOR will require significant detail.

Preliminary market engagement is permitted before any of the procedure routes and allows you to informally gather informationto help you understand the current position of the market, gather ideas on new products and services and to understand if there are any market developments that influence your requirements.
It’s important that any supplier contacted for pre-market engagement understands that you will still be following the G-Cloud buying process under the PA23 regulations once the procurement begins.

Remember that you should keep a record of all pre-market engagement activities and you must ensure that no supplier has gained an unfair advantage through the engagement that could distort the process.

Objective Mechanism for Awarding without Competition in G-Cloud 15
High Level Description
Stage 0.
The buyer will identify the Lot that their requirement will be in scope of, and access the digital platform for that Lot.
Stage 1.
The buyer will apply filters through the digital platform in order to reflect the high-level requirements identified in their Statement of Requirements (SOR).
Stage 2.
The buyer will review the Digital Platform Item Information to further filter suppliers against the detailed elements of their Statement of Requirements (SOR).
Stage 3.

Having identified all suppliers capable of meeting their detailed Statement of Requirements (SOR), the buyer will review the mechanism for establishing price identified by the framework, and will award to the supplier with the lowest price.
DetailedDescription
Stage 0.
The buyer will identify the Lot that their requirement will be in scope of, and access the digital platform for that Lot.
If their requirement is for above-OFFICIAL classified use–choose Lot 1b
For any other requirement, if itrequires Infrastructure or Platform ‘as a service’ only – choose Lot 1a
If the requirement is for Software ‘as a service’ AND Cloud Support – Choose Lot 2a for infrastructure related software, or Lot 2b for user-application software
If the requirement is for Software ‘as a service’ ONLY – Choose Lot 2a for infrastructure related software, or Lot 2b for user-application software
If the requirement is for Cloud Support ONLY – Choose Lot 3
Stage 1.
The buyer will apply filters through the digital platform in order to reflect the high-level requirements identified in their SOR.

See Annex 2 Digital Platform Information (part 3)
Stage 3.

Having identified all suppliers capable of meeting their detailed SOR, the buyer will review the mechanism for establishing price identified by the framework, and will award to the supplier with the lowest price.

Pricing for the service line provided within the pricingdocument attached to that service line/catalogue entry, less the Framework Discount for that contractual value

The lowest Price when calculated according to the following mechanism;

Procedure for Awarding with Competition in G-Cloud 15
Two Stage Competitive Procedure
High Level Description
Stage 0.
The buyer will identify the Lot that their requirement will be in scopeof, and access the digital platform for that Lot.
Stage 1.

The buyer will apply Conditions of Participation (CoP) through the digital platform (using the platform filters) in order to reflect the high-level requirements identified in their Statement of Requirements (SOR).
Stage 2.
The buyer will invite all shortlisted suppliers to respond to a tender based on a Statement of Requirements (SOR) using a Request for Proposal procedure that they define.
Multi Stage Competitive Procedure
High LevelDescription
Stage 0.
The buyer will identify the Lot that their requirement will be in scope of, and access the digital platform for that Lot.
Stage 1.
The buyer will apply Conditions of Participation through the digital platform (using the platform filters) in order to reflect the high-level requirements identified in their SOR.
Stage 2 onwards.

The buyer will make use of any of the available optional modules in any number and configuration in order to arrive at a clear award decision. This may involve further review of the Digital Platform Item information, and/or using a Request for Proposal procedure that they define.
Contractual Information (Terms and conditions)

It consists of:
General terms
Core T&Cs that cover all call offs let under the PSC: payment, liabilities, termination, dispute resolution
Framework Award Form

Joint Schedules (14)
These terms apply to both Framework and any Call Off let under it - Definitions, Variation Form, Key Subs, Guarantees.

For GDPR within G-Cloud 15 please seeJoint Schedule 10 - processing data.
National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)
The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is the UK’s national technical authority for cyber security incidents. The NCSC offers assurance that covers a wide range of services like:
●NCSC Certified Consultancy Scheme which includes riskmanagement, risk assessment, security architecture and audit and review
●Penetration testing (CHECK)
●Cyber Incident Response (CIR)
●Certified training
●Certification (cyber essentials)
Customers purchasing services offered by the NCSC certified supplierscan be assured that they meet the National Authority’s technical standard. The benefits of using an NCSC assured supplier are:
●the supplier will have met the NCSC’s standards and can be trusted to act in NCSC’s name
●the supplier will have a proven trackrecord in delivering high quality consultancy services to customers
●they will have demonstrated a defined process for working with customers to understand their needs and tailor advice accordingly
●they will have demonstrated a clear understanding of current and potential cyber threats, techniques, and effective mitigations
●the supplier will continuously seek to improve the services offered to meet the evolving needs of the customer

The NCSC has recently publishedadditional guidanceon ensuring due diligence when procuring SMS suppliers. The NCSC's updated guidance on SMS best practices and as such they would advocate that suppliers:
●Adhere to theA2P Code of Conduct.
●Transparently share downstream providers.
●Actively participate in the MEF Registry to combat smishing and spoofing.
●Provide data on SMS routing for effective distinction between legitimate and fraudulent messages.
●Adhere to contractual obligations, emphasising that in instances of fraud, financial liabilities will not be assumed, underscoring the commitment to fair and secure business practices.
We’d also like to remind suppliers of mandatory GDPR compliance, which ensures the protection of people’s personal data and safeguards against unauthorised access and data breaches.
To learn more about the relevant NCSC guidance please read the Business communications - SMS and telephone best practice guide
For more information on the services available, please visit theNCSC website.
Financial Viability Assessment
The Framework will require the Supplier’s monitoring of itself, the immediate parent, and the Guarantor.

In order tobetter protect Public Sector organisations against Supplier financial instability and potential collapse, and in compliance with the Outsourcing Playbook, G-Cloud 15 tests a Supplier’s economic and financial standing as part of theframework application process. This principle will remain in place throughout the life of G-Cloud 15 as perJoint Schedule 7. This Schedule provides GCA and the Buyer with the option of using Credit Ratings and/or Financial Indicators for the purposes of the Financial Distress Provisions. Buyers may use any combination of these indicators to suit their own requirements with regular checks and reviews conducted against those Suppliers successful in their application.

During the life of the framework agreement, should you fail to informus of a Financial Distress Event (FDE) as covered in 2.3.3 of Joint Schedule 7, GCA reserve the right to suspend your G-Cloud 15 services until a satisfactory resolution has been reached as covered in 6.1.1 of Joint Schedule 7.

Management Information (MI) reporting
As a G-Cloud 15 Supplier, you will be contractually obliged to provide monthly Management Information (MI) reports to GCA.
Suppliers are required to submit MI even if you have not got any business toreport you need to still report no business.
The MI report must be submitted by the fifth working day of each month through thereport management information system (RMI).
You must report on:
Eachorder (call-off contract) and/or variation and/or extension agreed with a customer. This must only be done:
once (not every month)
against the month within which it was agreed with a customer during the next available MI submission window
on the Contractssheet found in the MI template (shown in the screenshot below).
Each invoice raised or submitted to a customer against any G-Cloud 15 business conducted in the month after they occur on the InvoicesRaised sheet (shown in the screenshot below).
The Digital platform Service IDs within the template is validated by the RMI system and must follow the correct format, i.e. xxxx xxxx xxxx xxx OR xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx*** (where * denotes a space).
The format of the MI report template must not be amended.
Failure to submit Management Information (MI) reporting
If two (2) MI Reports are not provided in any rolling six (6) month period then anMI Defaultshall be deemed to have occurred and GCA shall be entitled to:

charge and the Supplier shall pay a "Default Management Charge"in respect of the months in which the MI Default occurred and subsequent months in which they continue, calculated in accordance with Framework Schedule 5; and/or
suspend the Supplier from the agreement until such time that deficient MIreports(s) are rectified; and/or
terminate the Contract.
The Default Management Charge shall be the higher of:

the average Management Charge paid or payable by the Supplier in the previous six (6) Month period or, if the MI Default occurred within lessthan six (6) months from the commencement date of the first Call-Off Contract, in the whole period preceding the date on which the MI Default occurred; or
the sum of five hundred pounds (£500).
If the Supplier provides sufficient Management Information torectify any MI Default(s) to the satisfaction of GCA and the Management Information demonstrates that:

the Supplier has overpaid the Management Charge as a result of the application of the Default Management Charge then the Supplier shall be entitled to arefund of the overpayment, net of any Admin Fees where applicable; or

the Supplier has underpaid the Management Charge during the period when a Default Management Charge was applied, then GCA shall be entitled to immediate payment of the balance as a debttogether with interest.
Management charge
You must pay GCA the management charge currently set at 0.75% of allcharges (excluding VAT) invoiced to customers.
We will invoice you for the management charge due each month based oninvoice-related MI values provided by you. You must make payment to uswithin 30 days from the date of the invoice.

The management charge applies to the full charges specified in eachinvoice raised and will not be varied due to any service credits or otherdeductions. For invoices raised by us, you must pay VAT on themanagement charge.
What happens if the Management Charge is not paid?
Payment of undisputed and valid GCA invoices should be completed within thirty (30) days. GCA may take action on outstanding invoices by:
issuing the supplier with reminders that an invoice payment is due and/or overdue;
charging statutory interest and charges on overdue invoices, as per the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998;
suspending theSupplier from the Framework Contract until such time that overdue invoices are paid; and/or
terminating the Contract.
Assurance
Suppliers must keep their service information on the Digital platform up to date for the term of the framework agreement.

At anytime throughout the duration of the framework, GCA and its agents reserves the right to review any claims that Suppliers made in their framework applications to verify that any information that was submitted is still an accurate reflection of their G-Cloud 15 service and that a particular service is within scope of the frameworkagreement.

If any service fails the assurance verification process, the relevant service will be suspended from the Digital platform. If it is unclear whether a service is within scope, GCA reserves the right to give a Supplier the opportunity to rectify the service information, but failing in that, that particular service will be removed from the Digital platform.
Where any of the following apply, there are a number of actions thatGCA may take, these include suspension or ending the framework agreement with a Supplier:
Supplier Financial Distress Event
MI Failures
renegotiating G-Cloud 15 terms and conditions
material Breaches of the framework agreement
provision ofcontingent labour and services inside IR35
persistent failure to perform as required by the framework agreement or under a call-off contract
encouraging Buyers to award outside of G-Cloud 15
replicating the service descriptions of another Supplier’s service lines
Audits

Suppliers may from time to time be subject to audits and are expected to use reasonable endeavours to provide audit information that is within scope without delay and provide auditors access to all relevant staff.

Suppliers must provide completed self-audit certificates to GCA annually to confirm that its systems, reporting and processing of public sector orders comply with the Framework contract as perFramework Schedule 8.
How Suppliers access and utilise theDigital platformduring the life of the framework agreement

Below is a summary of what changes can be made by you in the Supplier account while the agreement is live. Note, any changes made by you will besubmitted to GCA for review and are subject to our approval.
Suppliers Changes
Please seeFramework Schedule 7 Annex E Section 4.
Updating Company Information
Company information can only be updated by the G-Cloud team. Please contact the G-Cloud team on info@gca.gov.uk
Updating your contact details

You can amend your contact details thatappear on each of the G-Cloud 15 services by logging in to the Digital platform, clicking on Company Details, and then on ‘Change’ on the ‘what Buyers will see’ section.
Any changes made by you will be submitted to GCA for review and are subject to approval.
Change of trading / company registered name
Where your trading or company registered name changes but the DUNS number and Company Registered Number remain the same, you will need to submit a request to info@gca.gov.uk.
Changing the RegisteredCompany Name, Company Registration number and DUNS number.

Where the registered company name and registration number or DUNS number need to be changed, GCA will need to determine whether a novation needs to take place. You will need to submit a request toinfo@gca.gov.uk
Updating a service name, service description, features and benefits
You will need to log into the Digital platform and select the service you want to change from the G-Cloud services list, and click on ‘edit’ to change the relevant section,in a particular service.
You cannot materially change how the service works and may be asked by GCA to prove it is still the same service.
Any changes made will be submitted to GCA for review and are subject to approval.
Adding/updating accreditations andcertifications
It is important that you keep all service information up to date.
Suppliers can add or update accreditations and certifications within their Digital Platform Items (service offers) during the term of the agreement.
Any updates will needto be submitted to GCA for review and are subject to approval.
If the accreditation or certification is directly related to a filter within the Digital platform, GCA will activate the filter for future customer searches.
All requests must be sent toinfo@gca.gov.uk
Removing a service
You can see a list of the G-Cloud services in the Digital platform. To remove one, select it, scroll to the bottom and click the ‘remove service’ button.
Once actioned the service will not appear in the Digital platform
search results any more but will still be viewable in the service details in the account.
Any existing contracts to provide the service will still be valid.
The URL of the service will remain public but a banner will be added to the service page stating when you made the service unavailable.
Updating the Digital Platform Items (service offers) pricing document –
SeeFramework schedule 3: Framework Prices
Updating the servicedefinition document
Suppliers can update their service definition document where it does not constitute a material change to the service.

Suppliers can update service definition documents by logging into the Digital platform. The Supplier needs to select the service for which they want to update from the list of G-Cloud services, click on ‘edit’ in the documents section of that particular service, select the document to upload, and click on Save and Return.
Please note pricing is not permitted on the service definition document. If this is found you will be asked to remove it or risk suspension of the service.
Any changes made by the Supplier will be submitted to GCA for review and are subject to approval.
Updating the Modern Slavery policy document

If your organisation has an annual turnover of £36m or more, you must comply with the annual reporting requirements of Section 54 of the Modern Slavery Act (2015) and provide a Modern Slavery Statement.
Customers may also choose to include Suppliers’ Modern Slavery Statements within their MAT (most advantageous tender) criteria when evaluating Suppliers’ services. More information onMAT.
To update your organisation’s modern slavery and human trafficking statement, please send it toinfo@gca.gov.uk
Adding/removing users to a Supplier account on the Digital platform
Suppliers can add or remove users ontothe Digital platform Supplier account by logging in and clicking on Contributors and inviting or removing contributors from there.
Retrieving a lost password for your Digital platform account

Any G-Cloud 15 Supplier with a Digital platform account can retrieve a lost password by going to the login screen of the Digital platform, clicking on Forgotten Password, and entering the email address that they use to log into the Supplier account.
Reporting technical issues relating to the Digital platform
These issues may include login errors, 404 errors, submission errors where there was an attempt to make changes, etc. All queries of this nature need to be directed to info@gca.gov.uk
Social value criteria

PPN 002requires all central government departments to consider social value in their evaluation criteria. This agreement is focused on the following 4 missions and policy outcomes from thePPN 002 Social Value Model:
Mission:Kick start economic growthto secure the highest sustained growth in the G7 -with good jobs and productivity growth in every part of the country making everyone, not just a few, better off.

Policy Outcome 1: Fair work:that offers fair wages and good working conditions. Help people get a job, stay in work, and progress in their careers, with good employment opportunities across the country. Notes: Where there is a large proportion of labour costs in the contract, commercial teams should consider MACs in Outcome 1 as a priority
Policy Outcome 2: Skills for growth:supporting growth sectors and addressing skills gaps.

Policy Outcome 3: Resilient, innovative and flexible supply chains:Support economic growth through enabling resilient businesses, opportunities for small businesses and voluntary, community and social enterprises
Mission: Make Britain a clean energy superpower:to cut bills, create jobs and deliver security with cheaper, zero-carbon electricity by 2030, accelerating to net zero
Policy Outcome 4:Sustainable procurement practices: reducing carbon footprints, minimising waste, and promoting the use of clean energy and green technologies.
[Policy Outcome 5 is intentionally omitted].
Mission: Break down barriers to opportunity:by reforming our childcareand education systems, to make sure there is no class ceiling on theambitions of young people in Britain
Policy Outcome 6:Employment and training for those who face barriers to employment
Policy Outcome 7:Creating a pipeline of opportunities for the contract workforce, reducing barriers to entry for under-represented groups.
Mission: Build an NHS fit for the futurethat is there when people need it; with fewer lives lost to the biggest killers; in a fairer Britain, where everyone lives well for longer.
Policy Outcome 8:Increasing productivity through physical and mentalwellbeing: in the supply chain and communities in the relevant area.
We recommend that you discuss social value questions during pre-market engagement activities. For more guidance on how to evaluate social value checkGCA Procurement Essentials: Social Value.
Supplier responses to the social value questions will be assessed against the social value model2025-02-08 PPN 002 Guide to using the social value model.docx.
Remember that social value should:
be assessed based on quality, not quantity
be relevant to the contract or framework
be proportional to the contract value
not ask for cash lump sums
